approach: Derive the limit in code when the job is dispatched and store it on the Job record. AcceptedReading::allowed_paths() (briefs.rs) returns the reading's deliverable paths when a criterion matches a narrow, windowed phrase matcher, and None otherwise. The Job gets an optional allowed_paths field set at the literal in run/mod.rs (~994). A path-only helper outside_allowed_paths(allowed, changed) sits beside unchanged_planned_files and normalises with normal_path. It runs at two points: (1) producer_loop (run/producer.rs), after each report, where an outside file is sent back to the producer through send_back_text_scoped, which names each path and the criterion and says to revert, with one extra scope-only send-back; (2) the head of check_and_verify (run/mod.rs:1544), before the decision gate, CI push and verifier, where a diff still outside, or a resumed candidate that skipped the loop, closes the job as Failed with a SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX reason that retry_findings carries on. Round-3 changes: the test-only form now needs a window (finding 4); a deliverable ending in '/' is a directory prefix (5); nested runs are skipped at both points like the decision gate, and a resume test is added (6); end-to-end tests assert the stored record (7); end-to-end tests delete files through (path, None) fake edits (8). A job with no stored list is never checked. Only Rust, CHANGELOG.md and one row of docs/records.md change; no prompt, governance file or records/ file.

decisions.choice: Derive the allowed list from the accepted reading in code: AcceptedReading::allowed_paths(&self) -> Option<Vec<String>> and limiting_criterion(&self) -> Option<&str> (briefs.rs). The list is the deliverable paths with a leading ./ removed and duplicates dropped (a trailing / is kept), when some criterion matches limits_changed_files(text). None when no criterion matches or the reading has no deliverables.
decisions.reason: The reading says the limit is derived in code from the accepted criteria and deliverables, and the reader prompt has no token headroom. Methods on the existing view add no field to AcceptedReading, so its struct literals (send_back.rs:214, reading.rs:5922, run_pin_tests.rs:1047) do not change. An empty list is never stored because it would flag every file.

rejected.why: Out of scope: no new reader output field, no prompt edits.

rejected.why: The limit is the accepted reading's, not the planner's.

decisions.choice: Matcher limits_changed_files(text): lowercase the text and turn every non-alphanumeric run into one space, then match only windowed forms. (a) 'no file' or 'no files', then within 8 words 'outside', then within 8 more words changed/change/changes/modified/touched. (b) 'no other file(s)' then within 3 words changed/change/modified/touched. (c) 'only' then within 6 words 'may change', 'may be changed' or 'may be modified'. (d) revised for finding 4: 'test only' or 'tests only' (hyphen flattened to a space, so 'test-only' is the same) followed within 2 words by change, changes, diff, job, pr or pull request. The bare adjective never matches, and neither does 'test-only edits', so it errs toward not matching. (e) 'production', optionally 'code', optionally 'is'/'are', then 'unchanged'. The window sizes are named constants.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: form (d) in round 2 matched the bare word 'test-only', which the repository uses as a plain adjective (docs/design/structure-pass.md:24, 49, 82 'a test-only seam'; docs/decisions.md:2563; CHANGELOG.md:2378). Giving (d) a window like the others means each form needs a path or job word and a change word together. The request's example 'test-only, production unchanged' is still caught by (e), and 'test-only change/diff/job' by (d). A false match is costly because the list is only the deliverables; a miss only means the verifier catches it, as today. Round 2's repository non-matches stay non-matches: records-history.md:134, athena-v0.md:984, reading.rs:6598 and context-engineer.md:153.

rejected.option: Keep bare 'test-only' as a match
rejected.why: Matches 'a test-only seam' and 'the helper is test-only'; a correct diff would close as Failed.

rejected.option: Include 'edit(s)' in the (d) window
rejected.why: 'test-only edits in X' is the repository's own adjective use (CHANGELOG.md:2378); excluded so it stays a non-match, accepting a possible miss.

rejected.why: Not a code check, and needs a new reader field or prompt change.

Add a clause to the athena.job/1 row of docs/records.md (~92) saying it is optional and present only when an accepted criterion limits which files may change.

decisions.choice: Compare exactly, except that a stored entry ending in '/' is a directory prefix: outside_allowed_paths treats a changed path as inside when it equals a normalised entry or starts with an entry that ends in '/'. The doc comment on Job::allowed_paths, the dispatch 'scope' line, the CHANGELOG bullet and the scoped send-back text say the limit is the reading's deliverables, so a criterion that limits scope needs a complete deliverable list.
decisions.reason: Finding 5: deliverables carry a probability and lists can be incomplete; a deliverable such as docs/ would otherwise flag every file under it. The prefix rule is a few lines in the helper, with a pure test. The accepted reading still chooses the list, so no escape hatch is added beyond that.

decisions.choice: Make the scope visible. At dispatch, right after the 'dispatched ...' line (run/mod.rs ~1047), when allowed_paths is Some, print one line: 'scope      allowed paths: a, b (from criterion "...")'. The criterion text comes from accepted.limiting_criterion(), which producer_loop and check_and_verify both hold. The send-back text and the point-2 reason both quote the criterion.
decisions.reason: Without it the first sign of a limited job is a send-back or a Failed close. The criterion in the message tells the operator and the next producer why the limit exists.

decisions.choice: Check at two points, and skip nested runs at both, as the decision gate does (producer.rs:279 'self.nested.is_none()', mod.rs:1565). (1) producer_loop: compute the changed path list once from changes (producer.rs:268) outside the unchanged block, call outside_allowed_paths, add the result to the break condition (producer.rs:290) and to problems; not to report_problems (315), because the job ends before the verifier. (2) Head of check_and_verify: if recorded_checks.is_none() && self.nested.is_none() and a list is stored, compare closing.candidate.changes with it; on a hit call self.failure with a reason starting SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX, restore changed_paths, set verification_passed = None as the decision branch does (1572-1576), and return before push_ci_branch (1583). Order: scope gate first, then the decision gate.
decisions.reason: The request asks for the check before hand-off and again before verification. Point 2 stops a diff still outside after the loop's send-backs and a resumed candidate that never went through the loop (resume_candidate, mod.rs:523, reaches check_and_verify at the Checks stage with recorded_checks None). A nested run is judged by the outer job, whose own check sees the combined diff, so checking it against the outer job's list would be a second, wrong comparison; a job at the verifier stage with recorded_checks passed on its first run.

decisions.choice: Give an out-of-scope diff its own extra send-back: SCOPE_SEND_BACKS = 1, counted apart from send_backs (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS stays 1). The limit test at producer.rs:336 becomes send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS && !(!outside.is_empty() && scope_send_backs < SCOPE_SEND_BACKS). A send-back whose shared slot is free uses it; otherwise the scope slot is used. At most 3 producer runs, only for a job with a stored list.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 asks that an out-of-list change made after the first send-back is sent back again before the verifier; the shared limit of 1 cannot do that. For a job with no list outside is empty and the old branch runs.

risks.risk: A phrase match on an innocent criterion stores a list and blocks a legitimate diff, such as producer.rs and store.rs for this very job.
risks.mitigation: The matcher is narrowed to windowed forms that need a path or job word and a change word together, including form (d) after finding 4. The tests carry this job's 8 criteria, the four repository sentences and the test-only adjective uses as non-matches. A limiting reading with no deliverables stores nothing. The dispatch scope line and the criterion quoted in every message make a wrong match easy to diagnose.

risks.risk: deny_unknown_fields means an older Athena binary cannot read a job.json that has the new key.
risks.mitigation: The field is optional, skipped when None and defaulted when absent, so existing records parse (new test). It is written only for a limited job.

risks.risk: Changing the loop's send-back limit and break condition alters behavior for jobs with no stored list.
risks.mitigation: Both new inputs are empty for such a job, so the old branches run; the existing send-back tests (run_pin_tests.rs ~1336-1387, run/tests.rs ~2303-2480) must pass unmodified.

risks.risk: A job closed at the second check has no verification, so its reason might not reach the retry's producer.
risks.mitigation: retry_findings accepts SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX (tested), and the reason names each path, the criterion and the fix.

risks.risk: The fake reader's gate may refuse the extra criterion the end-to-end tests add, or the resume test (Test C) may not be driveable with the existing disk hook.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs cargo test -p athena-core scope_send_back and adjusts the wrapper only. If the reader's gate refuses the criterion or the resume case cannot be driven, the producer reports it, does not change the gate, and drops the resume test with the claim noted in its report.

risks.risk: The deliverable list omits run/producer.rs, store.rs and docs/records.md.
risks.mitigation: The plan names all three with reasons; the producer lists them in its report. The planned-files check flags only planned files left unchanged.

risks.risk: A window in the matcher is too tight or loose and misses a real limiting criterion, for example 'test-only edits'.
risks.mitigation: A miss only means the job is unchecked, as today, and the verifier still catches it. Each form has a positive unit test, and the windows are constants named in briefs.rs.

risks.risk: A deliverable list that is incomplete makes a correct diff fail the scope check.
risks.mitigation: Directory entries ending in '/' act as prefixes; the changelog, the doc comment, the scope line and the send-back text say the limit is the reading's deliverables.

demonstrations.method: Pure test plus end-to-end tests. The pure test calls outside_allowed_paths with a stored list and a changed list holding one outside path and asserts that exact path comes back; a second pure test builds the text with send_back_text_scoped from it. The end-to-end tests run whole jobs whose reader output carries a limiting criterion and whose producer also edits NOTES.md (an added file) and, in a second test, deletes a file outside the list with a (path, None) fake edit (finding 8).
demonstrations.observes: The helper returns the outside path by name. In the end-to-end test where attempt 1 is clean, the second producer prompt carries '## Sent back' and names NOTES.md, and the verifier runs once after the send-back. In the deletion test the deleted outside file is named in the second prompt. In the test where the diff stays outside, the verifier count is 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no check, outside_allowed_paths does not exist and the job reaches the verifier with one producer prompt. A check returning nothing fails the named-path assertion, and a check that ignored deletions fails the deletion test.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: crate::run::outside_allowed_paths (added by step 3, beside unchanged_planned_files) and Athena::go through producer_loop. Fixture: the existing counting/editing fake script (run/tests.rs:2152, 2234), governed_job_with (2263), athena_with (187), Counts and Lines. A wrapper script added by step 9 appends a limiting criterion to the fake reader's acceptance_criteria only and picks per-attempt edits, including (path, None) deletions, from the prompt vector, as reconciling_on_send_back does. It supplies input only; the logic under test is production code. The seam for the pure test is added by step 3; the wrapper by step 9.

demonstrations.method: Pure test plus end-to-end tests. The pure test passes outside_allowed_paths changed paths that are a './'-prefixed allowed path, a deleted allowed path, a plain allowed path and a path under an allowed 'dir/' entry, and asserts an empty result. End-to-end: a scoped job whose producer edits only README.md, and a scoped job whose producer deletes an allowed file with a (path, None) edit (finding 8).
demonstrations.observes: The helper returns an empty Vec. Both jobs reach the verifier with one producer prompt, verifier count 1 and no scope Failed outcome; the deletion job's change list carries the deleted path, so a real deletion goes through the check.
demonstrations.fails_without: A raw-string comparison flags './README.md'; a check that compared only added files would flag the deleted path; no prefix rule flags the 'dir/' case; an always-rejecting check leaves the verifier count at 0.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: outside_allowed_paths (step 3) and Athena::go through producer_loop. The end-to-end jobs use the scoped wrapper (step 9); change_list includes deletions (finding 8 cites athena-git snapshot.rs:200 via diff_tree), so the deletion is a real working-tree deletion made by the fake producer's (path, None) edit. The wrapper supplies input only.

demonstrations.method: Pure tests build readings with the accepted() builder (run_pin_tests.rs:1046), set deliverables on its public field and check allowed_paths(). Positive: a limiting criterion with deliverables ./a.rs and b.rs gives Some(["a.rs","b.rs"]) equal to the deliverable paths; 'No file outside X changed', 'test-only, production unchanged', 'test-only change in X' and 'only the docs may change' each give a list. Negative, None: each of this job's 8 criteria; the four repository sentences (records-history.md:134, athena-v0.md:984, reading.rs:6598, context-engineer.md:153); 'reached through a test-only seam', 'the helper is test-only' and 'test-only edits in the helper' (finding 4); a reading with no limit; a limiting criterion with no deliverables. End-to-end: an unscoped job whose producer edits README.md and NOTES.md, which also loads the committed records and asserts the job record's allowed_paths is None and that its job.json text has no 'allowed_paths' key; the scoped job's record holds the deliverable paths (finding 7).
demonstrations.observes: The stored list equals the deliverable paths for limiting readings and is None for the rest. The unscoped job has one producer prompt, one verifier run, no scope reason, no 'scope' UI line and no allowed_paths key in its record.
demonstrations.fails_without: A matcher that ignored criteria returns None for limiting readings and fails the equality. One that matched the repository sentences or the bare 'test-only' adjective fails the negative cases. One that matched everything flags NOTES.md in the unscoped job. A bug that stored a list but skipped the check fails the record assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: AcceptedReading::allowed_paths and limiting_criterion (step 1) and Athena::go. The pure tests use the existing accepted() builder. The end-to-end test uses the existing governed_job helper (run/tests.rs:2252), which takes extra producer edits, and reads the record through Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head().unwrap()) as the test at run/tests.rs ~3131 does; the producer confirms the field path to the Job (records.jobs[id].job). No double holds logic under test.

demonstrations.method: End-to-end tests with the scoped wrapper. Test A: the producer edits NOTES.md on attempt 0, a different file EXTRA.md on attempt 1 (after the first send-back), and reverts both on attempt 2. Test B: every attempt edits NOTES.md. Test C (resume, finding 6): a job is held at the Checks stage by low disk with an out-of-list candidate and no stored list (the reader adds the limiting criterion only from its second call on); the retry's reading then carries the limit, the retry resumes the kept candidate, and the head of check_and_verify closes it. Test D: a nested run is not checked, if the existing nested test harness can drive one cheaply; otherwise this is a code-reading claim only and the producer says so.
demonstrations.observes: Test A: three producer prompts, prompts[2] contains '## Sent back' and names EXTRA.md, one verifier run. Test B: three producer runs, verifier count 0, Failed outcome whose reason starts with SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX and names NOTES.md (point 2); the UI lines include 'files still outside the allowed paths after the send-back'. Test C: no producer or planner run on the retry, verifier count 0, Failed with SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX, no 'checks' lines. The producer should be ready to report failure if the reader gate refuses the extra criterion, rather than change the gate.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the extra scope allowance, attempt 1 hits the limit at producer.rs:336, so Test A has two producer prompts and the job closes at point 2; the three-prompt assertion fails. With no check in check_and_verify, Test B reaches the verifier (count 1) with no scope reason, and Test C proceeds to the checks.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: Athena::go -> producer_loop (point 1) and check_and_verify (point 2), reached from produce_and_verify (mod.rs ~1536) and resume_candidate (mod.rs:523). Fakes: the existing editing/counting scripts, plus a wrapper that picks the edit by prompt index and the reader output by call count. Test C reuses the low_while_checking disk hook and the low-disk-at-checks retry flow (run/tests.rs:3076-3149). Counts, athena_with and Lines exist; the wrapper is added by step 9.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in records.rs. One builds a Job with allowed_paths: Some(vec!["crates/a.rs","README.md"]) through the job_on helper, serialises with AnyRecord::to_json, asserts the text contains "allowed_paths", re-parses it and passes the bytes and canonical_path() to check_record_file. The other uses a Job JSON with no allowed_paths key and asserts check_record_file returns the record with allowed_paths == None and that re-serialising omits the key.
demonstrations.observes: The round-tripped record equals the original; the old-shape record passes the records check and re-serialises without the key.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, the new record fails deny_unknown_fields on parse. Without #[serde(default)] the old-shape record fails; without skip_serializing_if the old-shape text gains the key and the absence assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: check_record_file(path, bytes) and AnyRecord::parse/to_json. Fixture: the existing job_on helper (records.rs ~5118) next to a_job_keeps_its_dispatch_branch_through_a_round_trip (~5137). The seam exists today; step 2 adds the field.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs at the repository root, plus the refusal corpus to show no reading-gate behavior changed.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: All exit 0. The corpus run gives each case its expected outcome (case ids I read, such as dependents-complete-ci-reuse and user-decision, were not run by me, so I report no result).
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error in a missed Job literal (store.rs, reading.rs, records.rs, run/mod.rs), a clippy warning, or an existing send-back or retry test broken by a changed output would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Cargo's own harness; no doubles; the commands exist today.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the working-tree diff: only the listed Rust files, store.rs, run/producer.rs, docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md changed; existing tests are unchanged apart from allowed_paths: None in Job literals; nothing in athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, prompt files or records/.
demonstrations.observes: The path list matches the plan's files, with no governance, prompt or records/ file. cargo test --locked (criterion 6) passes, including the existing send-back and retry-finding tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: An edited prompt, config or records file shows in git status; a changed existing test expectation shows in git diff.
demonstrations.seam: git status and diff on the working tree; they exist today.

demonstrations.method: A pure test calls send_back_text_scoped with two outside paths and a criterion and asserts both appear as '- path' lines under the outside-paths heading, that the text quotes the criterion, says the limit is the reading's deliverables and contains the revert instruction, and that with a None scope the output equals send_back_text_full's. The CHANGELOG entry is read from the diff.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core scoped_send_back && git diff -- CHANGELOG.md
demonstrations.observes: Each offending path is named and the text says to revert it. CHANGELOG.md shows one new bullet under '## [Unreleased]' / '### Added' that names the stored allowed paths, the two checks, and that the limit is the reading's deliverables (so a directory entry ending in '/' covers a tree).
demonstrations.fails_without: A text that did not list the paths or did not say to revert fails the assertions; no changelog bullet means an empty diff for CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: send_back_text_scoped (added by step 4), called directly. The changelog check is a diff read. No doubles.

open_questions: User: Is the extra scope-only send-back (up to 3 producer runs for a job with a stored list) wanted? The alternative is the single shared send-back, closing the job at the second check, which saves a producer run but cannot send a second out-of-list change back.

User: Should the stored list also cover files a build always rewrites, such as Cargo.lock, for a limited job? As planned, any changed file outside the deliverables (and not under a 'dir/' deliverable) is flagged, which is what the request says.
